summary:
Chocó is a department of Colombia on the Pacific coast. It stands under Colombia's national framework, and the national record carries that layer. The source inventory contains no Chocó-specific legal provision, departmental policy, enforcement practice, or documented incident against a trans person.

The region-specific signal is armed-actor control. In Chocó, armed groups rather than the departmental police regulate conduct, and trans women are displaced from the department. The element of the national framework that bears on Chocó is protection for victims of armed conflict; the sources do not record how that protection operates inside the department.

No Chocó-specific homicide or violence count appears in the inventory, so no departmental figure can be set against the national one. The department is named in the sources only through the displacement claim and through the observation that armed groups, not the police, set the rules of conduct there.
tangentialFactors:
Documentation of armed-group flyer campaigns, named killings, court rulings on facilities and custody, and national homicide counts concerns Colombia as a whole or other departments; it is carried by the national record rather than here.

Chocó appears in the sources alongside other departments in the displacement claim. The sources do not rank departments or give Chocó a separate figure, so no comparison between Chocó and other parts of Colombia can be drawn from this inventory.
localsOnly:
No Chocó-specific resident-facing provision, service, or enforcement practice was identified. Residents fall under the same national framework as the rest of Colombia, including protection as victims of armed conflict.

The documented local condition is that armed groups rather than the departmental police regulate conduct, and that trans women leave the department. The inventory records no departmental programme, complaint mechanism, or police practice addressed to trans residents.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: no Chocó-specific homicide count, no departmental enforcement data, no record of how the departmental police handle complaints by trans residents, and no Chocó ruling on facility access or custody appear in the inventory.

Whether the national protection for victims of armed conflict is operational in Chocó is not sourced.
